newsitem.title: UK: UK sets probe into paedophilia in secure hospital.
newsitem.headline: UK sets probe into paedophilia in secure hospital.

text.p: The government on Monday launched a top-level inquiry into allegations of child molesting and drug use at a top-security hospital where some of Britain's most dangerous child murderers and rapists are held.

Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell told parliament the inquiry was ordered after a patient at the hospital alleged that drugs, pornography and alcohol were available and that a child was regularly molested while visiting the unit housing the most dangerous inmates.

Ashworth Hospital in Merseyside, northwest England houses about 600 of Britain's most notorious killers and psychopaths, including the so-called Moors murderer Ian Brady, jailed for life in 1966 for the murder of three teenagers.
Dorrell said the hospital's chief executive, a member of the medical staff and two nurses had been suspended and a young girl had been taken into local authority care.

"The allegations which have been made... are extremely serious," he said. "Ashworth Hospital must be properly managed and must provide a high level of security for the benefit both of patients and of the public at large."
Dorrell said the inquiry would be run by a recently retired senior judge, Peter Fallon, but would not compromise police investigations or any criminal proceedings.
An inquiry four years ago strongly criticised Ashworth's management for its oppressive, penal regime and led to the suspension of eight staff.
Tessa Jowell, deputy health spokeswoman of the opposition Labour Party, said the allegations exposed the dreadful inadequacy of monitoring systems at Britain's high-security hospitals.
